name: The Coastal Chain
description: Lighthouse coordinates survival signals along the African Atlantic coast. Three relay beacons need repair or replacement. Without them, settlements between Cape Town and Lagos lose their only emergency warning network.

stages.name: Repair Beacon Point Alpha — Namibia Coast
stages.description: The first beacon is on the Namibian coast near old Walvis Bay. It's been silent for six months. Lighthouse suspects physical damage rather than power failure.

stages.name: Repair Beacon Point Beta — Angola Coast
stages.description: The second beacon in Angola has been transmitting corrupted data. The Lighthouse needs clean signal restored — the settlement nearby depends on it for storm warning.

stages.name: Repair Beacon Point Gamma — Nigeria Coast
stages.description: The northern end of the coastal chain — a beacon near old Lagos that guards the approaches to the largest surviving West African settlement.
